_readme.covers: Units 27-32. Chromaticism: augmented sixth chords and their resolutions, Neapolitan chords and their resolutions.
_readme.structure: Every rule has: rule_id, tier, category, weight, error_message, check.

notation.neapolitan: Following Aldwell & Schachter, the Neapolitan is written N (root position), N⁶ (first inversion, by far the most common), and N⁶⁴ (second inversion, rare).
notation.augmented_sixth: It⁶, Fr⁴₃, Ger⁶₅ — the standard figured-bass labels used by the book.
notation.applied: V/x and V⁷/x for applied dominants; vii°/x, viiø⁷/x, vii°⁷/x for applied leading-tone chords.

not_implemented.Unit 27: Added-dissonance chords (9th, 11th, 13th) require the analyzer to recognise 5-note pitch-class sets. Deferred.
not_implemented.Unit 30: Altered dominants (V7b5, V7#5) and augmented triads are outside the analyzer's pitch-class vocabulary. Common-tone dim7 requires a new handler. Deferred.
not_implemented.Unit 31: Chromatic sequences and equal-division-of-the-octave patterns require a sequence-detection layer that the analyzer does not have. Deferred.
not_implemented.Unit 32: Modulation and chromatic tonal areas require a sliding-key architecture. Deferred.

how_to_add_a_rule: 1. Copy a rule block between { and }.
2. Give it a new unique rule_id.
3. Choose a check.type that a pass module has registered.
6. Save. No trailing comma after the last rule.

rules.error_message: Augmented sixth tendency tone did not resolve by half step — b6 must descend to 5, and #4 must ascend to 5
An augmented sixth chord must resolve to a chord containing scale degree 5 (V, V7, or I64)
The lowered second (b2) of a Neapolitan should resolve down to 1 or up to 2 — it did neither
The bass of N⁶ (scale degree 4) should normally ascend to 5, descend to 3, or continue to a chromatic sonority
